page.layout: Running head at the top; one column of text, with the first paragraph continuing from the previous page; a full-width rule; a centred paragraph below the rule; catchword at the lower right; a fleuron ornament below (not text).

main_text.p: cali Holem, quód illud supra sinistrum latus literæ signetur: ut [illegible, ~1 letter] ho,re via vero supra mediam literam, ut [illegible, ~1 letter] ha.

p.i: Lecturi praecepta prolixiora, videant Hebraicam Grammaticam Michaelis Neandri, Valentini Schindeleri, vel aliorum.

main_text.p: Hactenus artes purè Germanicè, Latinè, Græcè & Hebraicè loquendi, expositæ fuerunt: Agemus jam de Arte ornatè Germanicè, Latinè, Græcè vel Hebraicè dicendi, videlicet de Rheto-rica.

page.notes: The two Hebrew words in the first paragraph ("ut ... ho" and "ut ... ha") are printed Hebrew letters that I cannot read with certainty at this scan resolution; they are marked as illegible. The Hebrew glyph in "ut ... ha" carries a diacritic point. The line "Lecturi praecepta prolixiora" has a ct ligature, transcribed as "Lecturi". The ornament below the text is a fleuron, not printed text. The right edge of the page is cropped, so line ends on the right may be incomplete, although the words shown are complete. The "s" long s is transcribed as s throughout.
